passage: Our neighbour in the Chandigarh lane, Maria, had her mother-in-law staying, and I was at their door when the older woman said to Maria's four-year-old, Nilufar, "Give Dadi a kiss." Nilufar hid behind her mother's leg. I saw Maria crouch. "You can choose. A kiss, a hug, a wave or a high-five?" Nilufar peered out. "Wave." She waved. Her Dadi nodded and waved back, smiling, though her face fell a little. I don't know whether Nilufar was tired or shy, but she looked easier after that.

qa.q: What options did Maria give Nilufar?
qa.a: She offered a kiss, a hug, a wave or a high-five.

qa.q: What might Nilufar have been feeling when she hid behind her mother's leg?
qa.a: She may have felt shy or simply didn't feel like being kissed. The narrator can't be sure whether she was tired or shy.

qa.q: What could Maria do to help her daughter and Nilufar's Dadi?
qa.a: She can keep offering choices and explain to Dadi that a wave is welcome too, so that everyone feels respected.

qa.q: How might Nilufar's Dadi feel when Nilufar waves instead?
qa.a: She may feel a bit disappointed at first, which shows in her face, but she still smiles and waves back.

grounding: A preschooler learns that hugging or kissing is a choice, and accepting a wave teaches that her body belongs to her.

passage:
Day one: at a family party in Coimbatore, Keerthana, five, was asked to hug her uncle. She shook her head and held out her hand. Her father Sahil said, "A handshake is fine."
Day four: her cousin asked, "Can I have a hug?" Keerthana said, "Yes," and they hugged.
Day seven: her grandmother arrived and said, "Come!" Keerthana said, "Can we do a high-five?" Grandmother grinned, and they slapped hands.

qa.q: What did Keerthana offer her uncle instead of a hug?
qa.a: She held out her hand.

qa.q: What does Keerthana's yes on day four suggest about how she felt?
qa.a: It suggests she was happy to hug her cousin because she was asked first. Her shake of the head on day one shows she can decide for herself, without meaning she dislikes her uncle.

qa.q: What should adults keep doing to protect the child's sense of control?
qa.a: They should keep asking before hugs, accept a handshake or high-five and thank the child for telling them.

qa.q: How might the grandmother feel about a high-five?
qa.a: She may be pleased that Keerthana still connects with her, and she grinned, so the high-five worked.

grounding: A preschooler learns hugging is a choice, and adults who accept a wave or high-five teach that her body belongs to her.

passage: The train would leave in five minutes. Deepak Mama bent down on the crowded platform. “Raghav, give Mama a kiss goodbye!” Raghav leaned back and shook his head. People jostled past with bags. His mother said, “Raghav can choose. Hug, wave or high five?” Raghav held up his palm. Deepak Mama slapped it, grinning. “Best high five in Pune!” He climbed aboard and waved from the door. Raghav waved back with both hands until the train was gone.

qa.q: What did Raghav choose instead of a kiss?
qa.a: A high five.

qa.q: What was Raghav feeling when he leaned back and shook his head?
qa.a: He didn't want to kiss and felt uncomfortable being asked, possibly also rushed and crowded on the busy platform.

qa.q: What did Raghav's mother do that taught him his body belongs to him?
qa.a: She gave him a choice of hug, wave or high five, even with a relative and little time.

qa.q: How did Deepak Mama respond, and what does it show?
qa.a: He accepted the high five happily, showing that love can be shared in ways the child chooses.

grounding: On a crowded platform, a preschooler chooses a high five instead of a kiss, and his uncle accepts it.

passage: Pranav ran to his friend Isha in the housing society park with his arms out, then stopped. His mother Kavitha had been teaching him to ask first. “Isha, can I hug you?” Isha shook her head. “No, I'm sweaty.” Pranav's arms dropped. He looked at Kavitha. She nodded. “You asked, and she said no. What else can you do?” Pranav thought. “Wave?” He waved. Isha waved back and grabbed his hand. “Come, let's go to the seesaw!”

qa.q: Why did Isha say no to a hug?
qa.a: Because she was sweaty.

qa.q: What was Pranav feeling when his arms dropped?
qa.a: He felt a bit disappointed and unsure what to do after Isha said no. Looking at Kavitha shows he wanted help.

qa.q: How did Kavitha help Pranav handle the no?
qa.a: She named what happened and asked what else he could do, so he found the wave himself.

qa.q: How might Isha see Pranav asking first?
qa.a: She likely feels respected and comfortable, since she could say no and still play with him.

grounding: A preschooler learns to ask before hugging and to accept a no, choosing a wave instead.

passage:
“Vasudha! Come here, give Bhavna Maasi a big kiss!”
Vasudha stayed by the door, holding the handle.
Maasi paused. “Hmm. Do you want a hug, a wave, or a high five?”
Vasudha thought. “…Wave.”
“A wave it is.” Maasi waved with both hands.
Vasudha waved back, smiling.
Later, her mother said, “Your Maasi loves you even with a wave, right?”
“Right,” said Vasudha. “Maybe tomorrow a hug.”
“Only if you want,” said Maasi.

qa.q: What did Vasudha choose?
qa.a: A wave.

qa.q: What was Vasudha feeling as she stayed by the door holding the handle?
qa.a: She was probably shy or unsure and did not want a kiss yet. Later she felt comfortable enough to smile and wave.

qa.q: How did Bhavna Maasi respond when Vasudha didn't come?
qa.a: She paused and offered a choice of hug, wave or high five, and happily accepted the wave.

qa.q: How might Vasudha's mother see Maasi's choice?
qa.a: She would likely be glad, because it teaches Vasudha that her body belongs to her even with relatives.

grounding: A preschooler chooses a wave instead of a kiss with her aunt, and the aunt accepts it.

passage:
Pickup note from Hafsa, Friday

Wasim's Nanu came to collect him today. He bent down and said, "Kiss for Nanu?" Wasim stepped back and held his school bag in front of him. Then he looked at me.

Last week we practised choices for greetings, so I said, "Wasim, you can choose." Wasim held up his hand. "High-five?"

Nanu laughed and gave him the biggest high-five. "Good one!"

Wasim walked out holding Nanu's hand, chatting all the way. Please keep offering him choices at home too.

qa.q: What did Wasim hold in front of him when he stepped back?
qa.a: His school bag.

qa.q: What was Wasim feeling when he stepped back and looked at Hafsa?
qa.a: He was probably unsure and a little uncomfortable about giving a kiss, and looked to Hafsa for support. Once he had a choice he seemed relieved and happy, chatting all the way out.

qa.q: Why was the high-five a good outcome?
qa.a: Wasim chose how to greet, and Nanu accepted it warmly, which teaches Wasim that his body belongs to him even with family.

qa.q: How does Nanu respond to being offered a high-five instead of a kiss?
qa.a: He laughs and gives the biggest high-five, showing he is happy to greet Wasim in the way Wasim chooses.

grounding: It shows a preschooler choosing a high-five instead of a kiss with a relative and an adult accepting it, teaching that his body belongs to him.
